subject.title: Feature: Allow cron heartbeat interval to vary based on state conditions (deadline-aware scheduling)

question: Should OpenClaw core add a state-aware cron/heartbeat cadence contract, and should it be expressed as conditional schedules, a scheduler hook/API, or deferred to plugin-owned orchestration?
rationale: The requested behavior changes public scheduling semantics and persisted config shape, and current code has adjacent but incomplete alternatives such as command cron jobs, heartbeat tasks, and cron lifecycle hooks.

options.title: Design core conditional cadence
options.body: Approve an additive core scheduler contract with safe predicates, named state sources, persisted schema/protocol changes, docs, migration handling, and cron/heartbeat coverage.

options.title: Route through hooks or plugin API
options.body: Keep static intervals in core and expose only the missing hook or plugin seam needed for external schedulers to adjust or requeue work safely.

options.title: Defer and document workarounds
options.body: Keep the issue open as a known product gap and document separate cron jobs, command cron gates, or HEARTBEAT.md tasks as the supported interim path.

recommendation.title: Design core conditional cadence
recommendation.body: Approve an additive core scheduler contract with safe predicates, named state sources, persisted schema/protocol changes, docs, migration handling, and cron/heartbeat coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature crosses cron scheduler state, heartbeat cadence, public protocol/docs, and prior area work where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
